auditor_tom: Morning. For SOC2 evidence we need a single trace for the 2024-06-11 emergency rotation: what changed in RBAC, who kicked the KMS rotate, and proof of artifact integrity. Can you assemble the control crosswalk for A.9 and A.12 mappings?

lee: Hey @auditor_tom 	611 incident summary: pipeline B leaked a short-lived deploy token -> we triggered emergency rotation of alias 'alias/redwood-incident-2' at 2024-06-11T02:40:10Z. RBAC change was limited: svc-deployer-prod had role/maintainer removed at 02:35 and re-added at 03:05.

ana: I performed the approval in the internal approval UI (ticket SEC-2024-099). Approval log: "ana APPROVE 2024-06-11T02:36:04Z - emergency rotate." Attached audit-id: audit-9099.

devops-bot: runbook-started: id=rb-20240611-08, initiated_by=manual, awaiting-approval.

lee: Commands to reproduce exports we've attached to the bundle:
Splunk scope: `search index=prod_audit event.type=token_use token_id="tk-deploy-zz" | table _time user host action`
CloudTrail KMS rotates: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=ReEncrypt --start-time 2024-06-11T02:30:00Z --end-time 2024-06-11T03:00:00Z`

ana: KMS line from cloudtrail we exported: `2024-06-11T02:40:10Z | arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ops-runner/session | RotateKey | arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/zzzz-1111-2222`

lee: RBAC change record snapshot: `change_id=rbac-8099 actor=lee target=svc-deployer-prod before_roles=[maintainer,exec] after_roles=[viewer,exec] start=2024-06-11T02:35:12Z revert_scheduled=2024-06-11T03:05:00Z ticket=SEC-2024-099`

ana: Runbook stdout (snippet):
[02:36:10] rb-20240611-08: awaiting approval
[02:36:04] ana: approve
[02:37:05] rb-20240611-08: invoking kms:RotateKey alias/redwood-incident-2 -> key/zzzz-1111-2222
[02:40:10] rb-20240611-08: RotateKey OK; publishing manifest to s3://audit-evidence/20240611/incident-099/
[02:42:00] rb-20240611-08: rewrap tokens in token-store: processed=128 errors=0

lee: Evidence manifest sample line: `token-store-rewrap.log sha256:9c1d5f3a2b4e6d7c8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a size:12KB uploaded_by:rb-20240611-08 uploaded_at:2024-06-11T02:42:10Z`

auditor_tom: For chain-of-custody, we need signatures and object lock info. Where are those stored?

ana: All evidence objects go to s3://audit-evidence/ with bucket-level object-lock (governance) and we store manifests signed by CI signing key (CI-SIGN-KEY-01). EvidenceLedger also records a ledger entry per upload with ledger-id e-ledger-2024 and we can export ledger CSV.

lee: CSV checksum (splunk export): `2f8e7b6c5d4a3f2e1b0c9d8e7f6a5b4c3d2e1f0a9b8c7d6e5f4a3b2c1d0e9f8`

devops-bot: integrity-scan complete for s3://audit-evidence/20240611/incident-099/ - checksums match manifests, signatures present.

ana: Control crosswalk plan: map A.9.1 -> rbac-change.json, A.9.2 -> approval-ticket-SEC-2024-099.pdf, A.12.3 -> cloudtrail-rotate.json and token-store-rewrap.log, evidence CSV and manifest sha. We'll generate a one-page PDF index that lists control->file->sha256.

auditor_tom: Good. One more: show proof that rotated key was not used to re-encrypt customer blobstore (we can't rewrap blobstore).

lee: Confirmation: blobstore uses separate CMK alias 'alias/redwood-blob' (key id k-blob-444). No rewrap job ran for that alias. CloudTrail shows no ReEncrypt events for k-blob-444 in the timeframe. We'll attach a CloudTrail filter result file.

ana: ETA for assembled bundle (zipped): 2024-06-11T20:00 PDT. We'll upload to s3://evidence-audit-delivery/auditor_tom/SEC-2024-099/ and post presigned link with 7-day expiry.

auditor_tom: Thanks. Please include the signed manifest and ledger export. Tag me when uploaded.

lee: will do. tagging @evidence-ledger to push ledger export.

evidence-ledger: export ready: ledger-export-SEC-2024-099.csv sha256:5b2a1c3d4e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2
